significance.note: The abstract states no sigma significance figure; none is recorded.

summary.plain: LSND counted an excess of electron-antineutrino events above the expected background in a beam of muon-antineutrinos, and interpreted it as evidence for neutrino oscillations (neutrinos changing type). The collaboration's own title calls this evidence.
summary.technical: LSND search for ν̄μ→ν̄e oscillations with ν̄μ from μ+ decay at rest (the paper's introduction calls these the final results using all the data): a total excess of 87.9 ± 22.4 ± 6.0 events consistent with ν̄e p → e+ n scattering was observed above the expected background, corresponding to an oscillation probability of (0.264 ± 0.067 ± 0.045)%. In conjunction with other known limits, the paper says the data suggest oscillations in the 0.2–10 eV²/c⁴ Δm² range, indicating a neutrino mass greater than 0.4 eV/c².

title: Evidence for Neutrino Oscillations from the Observation of Electron Anti-neutrinos in a Muon Anti-Neutrino Beam
why_it_matters: The paper notes that it is difficult to explain the solar neutrino deficit, the atmospheric neutrino anomaly and the LSND excess with only three flavours of neutrinos, so that a fourth, sterile neutrino has been proposed to explain all of the data.
